# Epic: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

## Problem

The shipped attract/demo bot (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ and its follow-ups) is a
per-frame priority ladder with a reaction-time governor bolted on. It has no
commitment, no forward model, no aim/fire reasoning and no way to learn from
human play, so it reads as random and cannot be tuned into competence. We need
a **maintainable bot framework** that plays competently and human-like, adapts
to new content (enemies, power-ups, weapons) without a rewrite, can be re-run
headless for reproducible evaluation, and is backed by **telemetry** gathered
both from our own recordings and from production playtesters.

## Goals / user stories

- **As the maintainer**, I can re-run the bot headless on a fixed seed and get
  reproducible results, so I can improve it safely.
- **As the maintainer**, I can add a new enemy / power-up / weapon and have the
  bot handle it through configuration, without touching the core.
- **As the maintainer**, I can record human play and analyse it (reaction
  times, target choices, engagement distances, dodge behaviour) to tune and
  evaluate the bot.
- **As the maintainer**, I can enable opt-in telemetry in production and gather
  playtester data (state + input + events) to improve the bot and the game.
- **As a player**, I see an attract/demo mode that looks like a competent
  player.

## Design overview

- **Determinism.** A per-run **seed** drives all gameplay RNG (wave/spawn/
  timing) so a run is reproducible and the bot can be evaluated same-seed.
- **Telemetry.** A **versioned, consent-gated, pluggable** pipeline. Records
  are per-tick state + input + discrete events, tagged with the run seed and a
  schema version. Sinks: a local JSONL dev sink and a production remote sink.
  No PII; **disabled by default in production**, opt-in only.
- **Bot framework.** A world model (from `BotSnapshot`), a **registry of
  goals/behaviours**, a **utility selector with commitment/hysteresis**, a
  behaviour-tree executor, and predictive **dodge/aim** behaviours.
  Content-specific parameters live in a **config/registry** so new content is
  data, not code.
- **Evaluation.** Same-seed bot-vs-human runs, metrics, A/B comparisons and
  side-by-side clips.
- **Style matching (later).** Fit parameters or train a policy from recorded
  telemetry once the competent bot exists.

## Epic acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** Runs are reproducible from a seed; the seed is recorded in
  telemetry; a headless runner executes the bot for N ticks on a seed and
  produces a deterministic report.
- **AC2:** Telemetry is a pluggable framework with a documented, versioned
  schema, disabled by default in production and opt-in consent-gated; it
  records per-tick state + input + events with the seed and is a no-op when
  disabled.
- **AC3:** The bot is a structured framework (world model + goal/behaviour
  registry + committed selection + predictive dodge/aim), not a per-frame
  priority ladder; new enemies/power-ups/weapons are handled via config with
  tests.
- **AC4:** The competent bot completes representative runs with human-like
  behaviour (goal commitment, no suicide, human cadence) and passes an
  evaluation report (survival, minerals/min, targets engaged, dodges).
- **AC5:** Human play can be recorded and analysed offline, and a replay/ghost
  viewer compares bot vs human on the same seed.
- **AC6:** Production telemetry can be enabled by a playtester via an explicit
  opt-in, with privacy documentation and no PII.
- **AC7:** All documentation is updated (framework, extension guide, telemetry
  schema/privacy); full suite, typecheck and build pass.

## Out of scope (this epic)

- A fully style-matched clone of a specific player (style matching is an
  early-phase deliverable; full fidelity is a later follow-up).
- Server-side ML training infrastructure or online multiplayer.
- CI wiring of the capture/eval jobs (follow-up once the harness exists).

## Children (dependency order)

1. Deterministic run seeding + seed plumbing.
2. Telemetry framework (versioned schema, pluggable sinks, consent flag).
3. Game telemetry instrumentation (per-tick state + events).
4. Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling.
5. Bot framework core (world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy,
   content config).
6. Structured competent bot (utility goals + behaviour tree + predictive
   dodge/aim).
7. Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons.
8. Same-seed evaluation harness (metrics, A/B, side-by-side clips).
9. Style matching from telemetry (parameter fitting / imitation).
10. Production telemetry (opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink, docs).

## Related work

Builds on AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ (Smart capture bot) and its follow-ups
AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB (human-like input) and AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L (movement
goals). Supersedes the per-frame priority-ladder design.
data.title: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

# Add 10% weighting to owned upgrades in hold-full choice

## Problem statement

When the hold fills and the player is offered a choice of upgrades, owned upgrades (weapon-level / power-up-level options) should appear 10% more likely than they currently do. Currently all candidates are selected uniformly at random; owned upgrades should receive a 1.1× weight multiplier.

## Users

- **Player (progression):** "As a player, when offered a hold-full choice I want a reasonable chance of upgrading an upgradeable weapon or power-up I already own, so my build keeps improving rather than forcing me to chase new items."
- **Designer:** "As a designer, I want owned upgrades to appear 10% more often so progression feels steady across runs."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — 10% weighting.** Owned level-up offers (both `weapon-level` and `power-up-level`) have a 1.1× weight multiplier applied during candidate selection. Unowned (base-pool) items retain 1.0× weight.
- **AC2 — Single source of truth.** The weighting logic lives in the strategy layer (`createRandomChoiceStrategy`), not in `buildChoiceCandidates`; no duplicate weighting code in scenes or gyms.
- **AC3 — Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every gym that opens the hold-full choice, because they share `MineralChoiceScene` and `powerups/choice`.
- **AC4 — Configurable weight.** The 1.1× multiplier is a named constant (e.g. `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT = 1.1`) so it can be tuned later without hunting for magic numbers.
- **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests verify: (a) owned-level candidates receive 1.1× weight; (b) weighted random selection produces the expected distribution (10,000 trials, ±3% tolerance, owned items appear ~10% more often than unowned items relative to pool size); (c) gym↔game parity tests pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour must live once and be consumed by both the game and every gym.
- **Backward compatible:** no breaking changes to the `ChoiceStrategy` interface or existing `ChoiceOption` consumers.
- **No gameplay logic changes beyond weighting:** the candidate list itself is unchanged — only the selection probabilities shift.
- **Run-scoped:** no leaderboard impact.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — add weighting logic in `createRandomChoiceStrategy`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — no changes expected (they already pass context).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — new tests for weighted selection (10k trials, ±3%).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — parity tests.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** — Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (completed).
- **AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J** — Weapon leveling (completed).
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship'\''s hold (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Statistical testing (low):** proving 10% bias requires many trials; tests use 10,000 draws with ±3% tolerance band.
- **Scope creep (low):** adding per-weight tunability (player-facing weight editor) could expand scope. Mitigation: this item implements a single constant only; per-weight tuning is a separate chore if needed.
- **Assumption:** "10% more likely" means a 1.1× multiplicative weight, not an additive 10 percentage points.
- **Assumption:** "owned upgrade" means `weapon-level` and `power-up-level` kind options in the candidate list.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope of owned upgrades?** (A: both weapon-level and power-up-level; B: only weapon-level; C: both with different weights.) — Answer (Producer): A — both weapon-level and power-up-level.
- **Q2 — Where does weighting logic live?** (A: in `buildChoiceCandidates` with tagged weights; B: in `createRandomChoiceStrategy` strategy layer.) — Answer (Producer): B — in the strategy layer.
- **Q3 — Test tolerance for statistical validation?** (A: 10,000 trials, ±3%; B: 50,000 trials, ±1%; C: 5,000 trials, ±5%.) — Answer (Producer): A — 10,000 trials, ±3%.
data.title: Add 10% weighting to owned upgrades in hold-full choice

# Intake Brief — Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old

## Problem statement

AI_Hell's enemy roster (E1–E7) is a coherent but self-contained set of
formations. It does not yet deliberately mine the **classic arcade era** for
signature, instantly-recognisable enemy behaviours. This epic researches that
era and turns the best candidates into implementable work items, so the game
can grow a distinctive "arcade homage" roster without ad-hoc, un-scoped enemy
requests.

## Users

- **As the game designer**, I want a researched, curated catalogue of classic
  arcade enemy behaviours adapted to AI_Hell's neon-vector rules, so that new
  enemy work starts from a clear design brief rather than a one-line wish.
- **As an implementing agent/developer**, I want each selected enemy to have
  its own work item with a user story, testable ACs, predicted key files and a
  plan that follows the existing data-driven enemy convention, so I can
  implement it without re-deriving the design.
- **As the producer**, I want the candidates that were considered but not
  selected recorded, so the roster can be expanded later without redoing the
  research.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A research document exists at `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` that
  catalogues **at least 5 and at most 8 selected** classic arcade enemy
  archetypes. For each it records: source game, the original behaviour,
  how it is adapted to AI_Hell's rules (neon-vector, code-drawn, no
  enemy–enemy collision), and why it was selected.
- The research document includes a **"considered but not selected"** section
  listing the remaining candidates from the research pool, each with a
  one-line reason for deferral, so the range can be expanded later.
- **One child work item exists per selected archetype**, each containing a
  user story, measurable/testable acceptance criteria (including unit tests),
  predicted key files, and a plan that follows §8.6 "Adding a new enemy" in
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`. Each child references this epic
  and the research document.
- Each selected archetype's design notes specify how it fits the data-driven
  pipeline — i.e. whether it is expressible as an `EnemyConfig`/CSV row or
  needs a new `src/entities/<Name>.ts` + factory/fire-dispatch seam — and give
  its **enemy difficulty scoring** inputs (movement / fire / health factors).
- Each selected archetype's notes name the **gym scene(s)** that will exercise
  it (existing `GymEnemies` or a new gym) to satisfy the gym↔game parity rule.
- Validation: the research document's recommendations are checked against the
  existing engine constraints (every selected archetype maps to an existing or
  explicitly-planned formation/shot-pattern registry entry), and every child
  work item carries explicit unit-test acceptance criteria.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Neon-vector aesthetic, code-drawn graphics only** — no external art assets
  (GDD §7.2).
- **Gym↔game parity** — an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a
  gym and the game; shared behaviour lives in `src/scenes/core/`. Enforced by
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs
  assertion (AGENTS.md).
- **Data-driven enemies** — tuning is data, not code; archetypes are rows in
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN). A genuinely new entity is
  only justified when the existing formation/shot registries cannot express it.
- **"Enemies are the bullets" design** (GDD §2.4) and **no enemy–enemy
  collisions** (GDD §2.6).
- **Behaviours must be adaptable to a top-down free-2D arena** — the original
  arcade games are lane/axis-based; the brief must state how each archetype is
  translated (or note where translation is not faithful).
- **Scope is research + design + child-item creation.** This epic does not
  itself implement the enemies; each selected archetype's implementation is its
  own child work item.

## Existing state

- **Enemy catalog** (GDD §4.1, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1):
  E1 Scout, E2 Diver, E3 Tank, E4 Phaser, E5 Swarm, E6 Asteroid, E7 Harvester,
  plus the multi-phase Boss.
- **Enemy implementation guide** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  documents the shared core scene library, the CSV pipeline (§8), and the
  "adding a new enemy" checklist (§8.6).
- **Data-driven pipeline**: `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`, `src/core/configTypes.ts`,
  `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`,
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`,
  `src/utils/enemyShotPatterns.ts`, `src/utils/formations.ts`.
- **Difficulty scoring**: `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` (absolute 0–100 index;
  movement/fire/health factors), pinned by
  `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`.
- **Gym surface**: single reusable `GymEnemies` scene + `GymIndex`; new CSV rows
  appear automatically.
- **Precedent**: E6 Asteroid (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F) is already an arcade homage
  built as a non-formation roamer with a split helper — a model for how far a
  new archetype may depart from the formation model.
- GDD §8 "Future Scope" already anticipates "Levels 6–10+ with new enemy
  types".

## Desired change

Produce researched, ready-to-implement enemy concepts drawn from classic arcade
games and capture each as a scoped child work item, with a shared research
document acting as the catalogue and the record of deferred candidates.

**Proposed candidate pool** (research selects 5–8; the rest go in the
"considered but not selected" section):

- Space Invaders — marching row that steps left/right and drops bombs.
- Galaga — entrance dive-in formation and tractor/capture beam.
- Pac-Man — ghost chase with distinct pursue/ambush personalities.
- Centipede — segmented chain that descends and reacts on segment destruction.
- Defender — fast attacker with a defined patrol/attack run.
- Missile Command — incoming falling projectiles / orbital strike telegraphed.
- Robotron 2084 — aggressive horde that swarm-steers toward the player.
- Frogger — lane traffic hazard crossing the arena (non-shooting obstacle).
- Joust — flapping momentum-based flyer in the top-down arena.
- Dig Dug — burrower that creates/changes traversal hazards.
- Q*bert — diagonal hopper with a fixed stepping pattern.
- Star Castle — concentric rotating ring shielding a core.

*(Every candidate in the pool is recorded in the research document; only 5–8
become child work items.)*

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` — New. The catalogue of selected and
  deferred archetypes (the epic's primary deliverable).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Updated. Add a reference to the
  research doc; each implemented archetype later updates the catalog (§1) via
  its child item.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Updated. Reference the research doc from
  §4.1 / §8 so the roster direction is traceable.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — Updated (by child items, not this epic). New
  rows for archetypes expressible as data.
- `src/entities/<Name>.ts` — New (by child items). Only for archetypes needing
  new entity code (e.g. burrower, segmented chain).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` / new gym scene — Exercised by child items for
  parity.

## Related work

- **Enemy Design tooling** (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN) — completed; the data-driven
  CSV pipeline new enemies plug into.
- **Asteroids as an enemy** (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F) — completed; precedent for a
  classic-arcade-inspired, non-formation enemy.
- **Enemy difficulty scoring** (AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K) — completed; every new
  archetype must supply its scoring inputs.
- **Extract common enemy base class for regular enemies** (AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52)
  — completed; the `BaseEnemy` seam new archetypes extend.
- **Data-driven enemy health config** (AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR) — completed.
- **Docs and README for enemy config pipeline** (AH-0MTHG5K6O008BCNJ) —
  completed.
- **Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md best-practice guide**
  (AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6) — completed; the guide §8.6 governs each child.
- **Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic** (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ) —
  completed; automated playtests must survive any new enemy, so its behaviours
  are a useful validation input for selected archetypes.
- **Alternative player control** (AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD) — completed.
- **Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments**
  (AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY) — completed; docs-update conventions to follow.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ** – Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic that seeks power-ups and minerals and dodges fire patterns (completed)
- **AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD** – Alternative player control (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: classic, create, drawn, dropping, eats (+23 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: arcade, classic, create, drawn, dropping (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: create, enemies, epic, era, etc (+17 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the research could expand indefinitely. Mitigation — cap
  selection at 5–8 this round; record all other candidates in the deferred
  section. Extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
- **Fidelity risk**: lane/axis-based arcade behaviours may need significant
  translation to the top-down free-2D arena; the brief requires each archetype
  to state its translation, and permits a documented divergence (per gym-parity
  rule).
- **Pipeline-fit risk**: some archetypes (burrower, segmented chain) cannot be
  expressed as a CSV row alone; the brief requires each to state whether a new
  entity/factory seam is needed before implementation starts.
- **Assumption**: the operator-supplied exemplars (Space Invaders row,
  Pac-Man ghosts, Centipede) are illustrative examples, not a required final
  selection.
- **Assumption**: "classic arcade era" means the coin-op era of the late 1970s
  to mid-1980s.
- **Assumption**: this epic's children implement the enemies; no separate
  implementation epic is needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "How many enemy concepts should this epic research and turn into work
  items?" — Answer (operator): **(A) focused set of ~5–8** from a named
  shortlist of classics. Source: interactive reply. Research: reviewed
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.6 and the existing 7-archetype
  roster; a 5–8 cap keeps the epic tractable and each child implementable.
- Q2 "Should the epic also produce a written research/design document, or only
  the child work items?" — Answer (operator): **(B) a dedicated research doc
  plus child work items**, and *"be sure to include other candidates not
  selected but considered so we can expand the range later"*. Source:
  interactive reply. Research: `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/intake` step 7
  and the repo's `docs/` convention; no existing research doc.
- Q3 "What should each per-enemy child work item include?" — Answer (operator):
  **(A) research + design + implementation of one enemy (full lifecycle in one
  child)**. Source: interactive reply.


---

## Plan

**Breakdown (created as child work items):** 1 research/validation child (R1)
+ 8 archetype full-lifecycle children (one per selected archetype) + 1
docs-integration child (D1). The epic itself does not implement the enemies.

**Selected archetypes (8):**

1. Space Invaders — stepping march formation.
2. Galaga — tractor/capture beam.
3. Pac-Man — ghost personalities (chase/ambush/flank/wander).
4. Centipede — segmented chain that splits on segment death.
5. Robotron 2084 — homing horde that swarm-steers to the player.
6. Defender — patrol-then-attack raider state machine.
7. Missile Command — telegraphed orbital strike.
8. Frogger — non-shooting lane traffic hazard.

**Considered but not selected (recorded in the research doc):** Joust, Dig Dug,
Q*bert, Star Castle.

**Test-first ordering:** R1 (research doc + automated engine-constraint
validation test) → E1–E8 (each a vertical slice: code + tests + code comments +
gym parity) → D1 (cross-cutting docs integration).

**Dependencies:** each archetype child depends on R1 (design brief must exist
before implementation); D1 depends on all archetype children (the GDD catalog
and guide must reflect the implemented roster).

**Phasing (vertical slices):** R1 is docs + validation test; each E* cuts
through the full layer stack (CSV/config → entity/factory/fire seam → shared
core → game + gym parity → tests → code comments); D1 is a cross-cutting docs
slice. Between phases, the next child's description is re-checked against what
was actually delivered and updated before implementation starts.

**Reused seams:** `BaseEnemy`, `EnemyConfig`/CSV pipeline
(`configStore`/`configCsvPlugin`), `formations.ts`, `enemyShotPatterns.ts`,
`enemyFire.ts` dispatcher, `AsteroidSpawner`/`HarvesterSpawner` (non-formation
spawner precedent), `GymEnemies`/`GymIndex`, `enemyDifficulty.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (planning)

- Q4 "When does the archetype selection get fixed?" — Answer (operator):
  **(A) fix the 5–8 selection now and create all children in this planning
  pass**. Source: interactive reply. Research: the epic's AC3 requires a child
  per selected archetype and the research doc's content is the same design
  brief, so fixing the set now avoids an extra planning pass and satisfies
  coverage immediately.
- Q5 "Which archetypes do you want selected?" — Answer (operator):
  **(A) select all 8 recommended** (Space Invaders, Galaga, Pac-Man,
  Centipede, Robotron 2084, Defender, Missile Command, Frogger); Joust, Dig
  Dug, Q*bert and Star Castle are deferred to the "considered but not selected"
  section. Source: interactive reply. Research: each selected archetype maps to
  a distinct existing/planned engine seam; the deferred four are weaker fits
  for a terrain-less top-down arena or overlap existing entities.
- Q6 "Breakdown shape for the children." — Answer (operator): **(A) a
  test/verification-first research-doc child (with an automated engine-
  constraint validation test) + one full-lifecycle child per selected
  archetype + a docs-integration child**. Source: interactive reply. Research:
  epic AC7 (README/GDD/guide) is cross-cutting and would otherwise be
  duplicated across 8 archetype children.
data.title: Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old

## Goal

Make the stored **Teleport** power-up activate **automatically**, the same way **Phase Shift** already does, instead of requiring a manual **S / ↓** key press. This removes the S / ↓ key conflict that blocks the reverse thruster (AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG) and frees S / ↓ for held reverse thrust.

## User story

As a player, when a hostile threat closes in and I hold a stored Teleport, I want the teleport to fire automatically (like Phase Shift) so I am not required to reach for a key in the middle of dodging — and so movement keys are never overloaded with a consumable ability.

## Background / existing state

- **Phase Shift already auto-triggers** through the shared, single code path: `CombatScene._updatePhaseShiftAutoTrigger(dt)` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`) calls the pure `isInDanger(player, bodies, bullets)` helper (`src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts`; danger when the combined hostile-threat count within `DANGER_RADIUS` is >= 3) and feeds the result to `EffectsRegistry.updateDanger(inDanger, dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`). The registry handles charge availability, re-arm-on-danger-cleared and a post-trigger cooldown, and plays the Phase Shift cue on activation. Every combat scene (game + gyms) calls this once per frame.
- **Teleport is manual:** `CombatScene._handleTeleport()` fires on `JustDown(teleportKey)` or the hardcoded ↓ fallback and calls `triggerTeleport()`, which consumes one stored Teleport stack (FIFO) and warps the player to the nearest safe spot along the heading, granting Phase Shift on arrival. Documented in GDD §4.4 / controls table as **S / ↓**.

## Expected behaviour

- Teleport auto-activates when the player is **in danger** (same danger definition/feed as Phase Shift) **and** a stored Teleport charge exists **and** the re-arm conditions are met (danger cleared since last trigger, cooldown elapsed) — mirroring the Phase Shift auto-trigger contract.
- Manual S / ↓ activation is **removed**; S / ↓ becomes available for the reverse thruster (AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG).
- Teleport keeps its existing trigger path: nearest safe spot in the direction of travel, consuming one FIFO stack, granting Phase Shift on arrival, and the existing Phase Shift activation cue plays.
- One shared implementation in the combat core so the game and every gym behave identically (gym↔game parity).

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — to be finalised by this item's own intake)

1. Teleport auto-activates via the shared danger feed when the ship is in danger, a Teleport stack is available, and the re-arm conditions (danger cleared + cooldown) are satisfied.
2. No manual S / ↓ (or `layerDrop`) activation of Teleport remains in the game or gyms; the ↓ fallback key is removed.
3. A stored Teleport is consumed exactly once per activation; stacking/FIFO semantics are unchanged.
4. The trigger uses the existing safe-spot + Phase Shift-on-arrival path; game and gyms share one implementation (gym↔game parity).
5. The re-arm/cooldown behaviour matches the documented Phase Shift model.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (GDD controls table, §4.4, any UI/HUD hints, code comments) — including the removal of S / ↓ for teleport.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes, with new/updated tests covering the auto-trigger, re-arm, and no-manual-key contracts.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — replace `_handleTeleport`/`teleportKey`/`downKey` with an automatic trigger fed by the shared danger feed.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — add Teleport auto-trigger state (charge check, re-arm, cooldown) alongside the Phase Shift model.
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` — reused as-is (shared danger signal).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` / `src/scenes/gym/*` — remove manual key wiring; ensure the shared auto-trigger runs.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — update the controls table and §4.4.
- Tests: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/RebindableControls.test.ts`.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Risk:** auto-teleport may fire more often than a player wants (each stored teleport is precious). Mitigation: match the Phase Shift re-arm/cooldown contract and make the trigger threshold explicit and testable.
- **Assumption:** "like Phase Shift" means the same danger-based auto-trigger model (not a timer), and the manual binding is removed entirely.
- **Blocker for:** AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG (reverse thruster on S / ↓).
data.title: Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift (free S / Down for reverse thrust)

# Add a GitHub link to the main menu

## Problem statement

Players and contributors have no way to discover the project's source code from the game itself.

## Users

- **Player/Contributor:** Sees the game on-screen, wants to find the repo to report bugs, contribute, or learn more.
- **Reviewer/Tester:** Needs quick access to the source during code reviews or gameplay testing.

### User stories

- *As a player who enjoys the game, I can click/tap a visible link on the main menu to open the GitHub repository in a new browser tab, without losing my game session.*
- *As a keyboard user, I can Tab to the GitHub link on the main menu and press Enter to open it.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Renders:** A GitHub link (`🐙  GitHub`) is rendered as text in the bottom-left corner of the main menu (`MenuScene`), below the subtitle and at the same Y position as the subtitle. It uses the existing `MENU_TEXT_COLOR` (#00ffff) with the same padding scheme as other buttons.
2. **AC2 — Click opens repo:** Pointer-down on the link opens `https://github.com/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell` in a new browser tab (`_blank`) with `noopener,noreferrer` flags.
3. **AC3 — Keyboard-accessible:** The link is registered with `FocusManager` after the Leaderboard button (Tab order: Play Game → Watch Demo → Settings → Leaderboard → **GitHub** → Gym Scene Index). Enter/Space on the focused link triggers the same action as a pointer click. Hover highlights the text in `#88ffff` (matching the existing pointer-over pattern).
4. **AC4 — Constant:** The URL is a single exported `const GITHUB_REPO_URL = 'https://github.com/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell'` in `src/core/constants.ts` (re-exported from `MenuScene` for testability), used as both the display label and the click target.
5. **AC5 — Tests:** Unit tests verify (a) the button renders with the correct label, (b) pointer activation calls `window.open` with the correct URL and target, and (c) keyboard activation via `FocusManager.handleKey` triggers the same `window.open` call.

## Constraints

- **Keyboard parity (GDD §2.1):** No mouse is ever required. The link must be in the Tab cycle.
- **No mouse required:** Use Phaser's existing pointer + keyboard interaction model; no DOM overlay.
- **New tab only:** Always use `_blank` to preserve the game session.
- **Existing pattern:** Must match the visual style of other menu buttons (neon-cyan text, dark background padding).
- **No `FocusManager` changes:** Reuse the existing manager; do not modify its public API.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` renders 5 controls: Play Game, Watch Demo, Settings, Leaderboard, Gym Scene Index (dev, bottom-right, fixed position).
- All 5 controls use `this.add.text()` with the same visual pattern (fontFamily: monospace, 20px, MENU_TEXT_COLOR, dark background padding).
- A shared `FocusManager` (`src/utils/focusManager.ts`) handles Tab/arrow cycling and Enter/Space activation.
- `window.open` has not been used in `src/` before; Phaser's canvas is the sole rendering surface.

## Desired change

Add a 6th control (`🐙  GitHub`) to the main menu:
- **Position:** Bottom-left, aligned near the bottom edge (X ≈ 16, Y ≈ GAME_HEIGHT − 12), matching the Gym Scene Index button's offset pattern.
- **Activation:** `window.open(GITHUB_REPO_URL, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')` on both pointer and keyboard activation.
- **Tab order:** Between Leaderboard and Gym Scene Index.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — Add the GitHub button (render, pointer handler, FocusManager registration).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — Export `GITHUB_REPO_URL`.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` — Add tests for the new button.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Popup blocker:** `window.open` must be called synchronously within the user-gesture event handler; otherwise the browser may block it. Mitigated by calling `window.open` directly in the pointer/keyboard handlers.
- **Tab order change:** Adds a 6th control to the existing 5. The order (Play → Demo → Settings → Leaderboard → GitHub → Gym Index) follows visual hierarchy (top→bottom, left→right).
- **Hardcoded URL:** The repo URL is a constant, not environment-configurable. Acceptable for a personal project; fork maintainers would edit the constant.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Where should the GitHub link live, and should it be keyboard-focusable? — Answer (operator): **A** — footer link, bottom-left, pointer-clickable and keyboard-focusable, appended to the Tab cycle. **Recommended** — keeps the GDD keyboard-parity contract intact.
- Q: How should activation behave? — Answer (operator): **A** — open in a new browser tab via `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')`. **Recommended** — preserves the game session.
- Q: Where should the URL come from? — Answer (operator): **A** — single exported constant (`GITHUB_REPO_URL` in `src/core/constants.ts`), used for both label and click target. **Recommended** — testable, single source of truth.

## Related work

- **MenuScene Settings button** (AH-0MUA8BLMA003U18N) — Similar pattern of adding a button to MenuScene.
- **In-game menu keyboard support (PauseScene)** (AH-0MUBZUQBL0080B88) — Keyboard navigation convention.
- **Add published game URL to top of README** (AH-0MUK3HYC3001YU05) — Same project URL, different location.
- **Create Main Menu scene** (AH-0MU72YVFR005VB2N) — Parent menu work.
data.title: Add a GitHub link to the main menu

# Retune boss HP to 200 and screen-fix the health bar

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want the Central AI boss to require 200 hits total (readable as 4 phases of 50) and I want its health bar pinned to the top of the screen so I can always read my progress regardless of where the boss is.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC1 and AC4.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE = 100` and `_totalHp = BOSS_PHASE_COUNT * BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE` (400 total). Doc comment and `BossConfig.initialHp` comment reference 400/100.
- `healthBarGraphics` is created with `scene.add.graphics()`, then `this.add(this.healthBarGraphics)` puts it in the boss **container**, so it renders offset by the boss position even though `_drawHealthBar()` uses screen coordinates and `setScrollFactor(0)`.
- `getHpFraction()` is already proportional and the four phase-segment dividers already exist — keep both.

## Desired change

1. Change `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE` to `50`; total becomes **200**. Update every comment/constant reference from 100/400 to 50/200 (including `BossConfig.initialHp` docs).
2. Remove the `this.add(this.healthBarGraphics)` container membership so the bar is a **scene child** (it is already created via `scene.add.graphics()`); keep `setScrollFactor(0)` and `setDepth(100)`. It now renders at the absolute screen coordinates drawn by `_drawHealthBar()` (horizontally centred at `BOSS_HEALTH_BAR_Y`).
3. Keep the proportional fill and the four phase-segment dividers.
4. Ensure `destroy()` still explicitly destroys `healthBarGraphics`.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — HP constants/comments, health-bar re-parenting.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts` — health-model and health-bar placement tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — gym health-bar placement expectations.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — health-bar layering assumptions if any.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE === 50` and total HP is 200; hitting 49 times keeps phase 1, the 50th hit advances to phase 2, and the 200th hit destroys the boss.
- The health bar Graphics is **not** a child of the boss container and its screen position is unchanged when the boss position changes (assert `boss.x`/`boss.y` separately from the bar's drawn position).
- `getHpFraction()` decreases monotonically with each hit from 1.0 toward 0.
- The four phase-segment dividers and the proportional fill are retained.
- All `Boss.test.ts` / `GymBoss.test.ts` assertions updated for 200 HP pass.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC1) **Boss total health is 200.** The boss spawns with 200 total hits across the existing **4 phases (50 hits per phase)**. The 4-phase structure, phase transitions, and score/minion rewards gated on *depleting* hits are preserved. Verified by unit tests: hit 49 stays in phase 1, hit 50 advances to phase 2, and hit 200 destroys the boss.
- (parent AC4) **The health bar is fixed at the top of the screen and decreases per hit.** The bar is camera-fixed, horizontally centred at the top of the playfield, always visible during the encounter, and **not** offset or moved by the boss's figure-8 motion. Its fill shrinks proportionally on every hit (200 → 0) with the four phase-segment dividers retained. Verified by tests asserting the bar's screen position is independent of the boss position and that `getHpFraction()` decreases after hits.
data.title: Retune boss HP to 200 and screen-fix the health bar

# Implement on-screen action intensity metric (recording + video join)

**Sibling epic** of the research/decision item [Screen action intensity
tracking and analysis (AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN)] —
`discovered-from:AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN`. Created by that item's AC5. This is a
sibling (not a child) so the research item can close once its decision is
recorded without waiting for implementation.

## Goal

Implement the hybrid layered `actionIntensity` metric decided in
`docs/dev/action-intensity.md`: a pure, deterministic, O(entities) score of
on-screen presence + event bursts, recorded through the existing telemetry
pipeline, serialised as a versioned time series, and joinable to captured
WebM for highlight selection.

## User stories

- **As a game designer**, I can view a time-series of on-screen action
  intensity for a run, so I can evaluate pacing and find boring or
  over-crowded segments.
- **As a video editor**, I can map action-intensity peaks to captured-video
  timestamps and auto-select highlight clips.
- **As a maintainer**, the metric is computed once in the shared core and
  consumed identically by the game and the gyms, and reuses the telemetry
  pipeline rather than a parallel instrumentation path.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Pure core module.** A pure `computeActionIntensity(state, config)`
  lives in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`), is O(entities) + O(1) per
  event, introduces no RNG, and returns the sample shape (rawScore,
  intensity, smoothed, burstiness, per-category breakdown) defined in the
  decision document §7.1. Unit-tested hermetically (no browser).
- **AC2 — Config.** All knobs (per-category weights incl. the refined
  player-bullet 0.5 and asteroids 1.0; `cap_c`; event window `W`; reference
  budget `B`; blend `k_E`; half-life `h`; sample rate) are config-driven with
  the decision-document defaults, and documented at the definition site.
- **AC3 — Telemetry integration.** The metric is wired into the per-tick
  telemetry `state` via the instrumentation child (AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH),
  reusing the `BotSnapshot` builder's registries. Recording is a **strict
  no-op when telemetry is disabled** (zero records, no allocation). No new
  schema bump is required (payload-only change); the shape is documented in
  `docs/TELEMETRY.md`.
- **AC4 — Event-window layer.** The burst layer consumes the discrete events
  the instrumentation child records (`enemy_killed`, `player_hit`,
  `boss_phase`, `powerup_collected`, `wave_clear`), with the documented
  default event values; verified by tests over a seeded event sequence.
- **AC5 — Derived time series.** A tooling-side serialiser emits the
  standalone JSONL artefact (`schemaVersion`, `runSeed`, `sampleRateHz`,
  `categories` header + one sample per line, `t` in ms since run start) to a
  git-ignored location alongside the capture output, with a matching
  basename. Round-trip tested.
- **AC6 — Video join + highlight selection.** A dev-gated `capture_started`
  marker (epoch ms, `import.meta.env.DEV`) is emitted at recording start; a
  helper maps `t` to video time using the shared anchor and returns merged
  highlight windows from the documented thresholds. Pure and unit-tested.
- **AC7 — Gym↔game parity.** The counter is authored once in the shared core
  and consumed by `PlayScene` and the gym scenes; the duplicate-body guard
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes. A single
  count-able registry (or per-kind live counters) exists for enemy/boss
  explosion VFX so categories are not double-counted.
- **AC8 — Docs & tests.** `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` is cross-linked from
  `README.md` and `docs/TELEMETRY.md`; the full suite, typecheck and build
  pass; no shipped-bundle impact (`npm run check-bundle` passes).

## Dependencies

- **Epic AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4** — Realistic demo/attract bot framework +
  playtester telemetry (must be at least `high`; verified).
- **AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO** — Telemetry framework: versioned schema, pluggable
  sinks, consent flag (provides the envelope/sinks; completed).
- **AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH** — Game telemetry instrumentation: per-tick state and
  events (canonical integration point; `actionIntensity` field lives here).
- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** — Automated gameplay capture spike (video consumer
  for the join).

Implementation must wait for AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH's tick-state integration
point to land (or land first if sequenced ahead of it).

## Key files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — the decision this epic implements.
- `src/scenes/core/` — new pure `actionIntensity` module + config (+ tests).
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — existing registries the metric reads.
- `src/telemetry/` — recorder integration (via AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH);
  `docs/TELEMETRY.md` schema note.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` / `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` —
  `capture_started` marker + highlight-selection helper.
- `README.md` — cross-link to the decision document.

## Out of scope

- Driving pacing / adaptive difficulty from the metric (separate consumer
  work item).
- Calibration against human/physiological data (separate follow-up; required
  before the metric drives difficulty).
- ML excitement prediction and automatic editing.
data.title: Implement on-screen action intensity metric (recording + video join)
